prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a near dark door/wall structure dominating frames 1–3, with the open room and people several metres behind it; brightness ordering appears locally inconsistent with the stated brighter-nearer convention, so metric estimates are uncertain. In frame 2, two people are visible through the opening at roughly 1–3 m from the camera wearer and about 1 m apart in depth, with the larger person on the right closer than the smaller person left/rear; by frame 3, the right person has approached to roughly 0.5–1 m while another person remains about 2–3 m behind. In frames 4–5, the nearest person fills much of the view at approximately 0.3–0.8 m, with extended arms reaching across the frame and therefore likely within the camera wearer's arm's reach, while a background person remains several metres away and is partly occluded. Compared with RGB, the map separates foreground bodies, doorway planes, and the deeper room more clearly, but flattened body regions, merged boundaries, saturation on the left wall, and unstable tone-to-distance relationships make exact distances and thin structures unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates people from the black background: none are detected in frame 1, two separate people appear near the center-right in frame 2, and at least two are detected in frame 3, with the nearer right person partly overlapping and occluding a smaller person behind-left. In frame 4, a large central person occupies most of the foreground with arms extended left and right, while a smaller person at far left and a small lower-right fragment are only partly visible; in frame 5, the foreground person is cropped by the top and right edges, with one raised arm entering from the upper left and another person's narrow fragment near center. The growing mask sizes across frames 2–5 show the principal person approaching from several metres to within roughly 1 m, while the other people remain farther back and become increasingly occluded. The map makes instance extent, overlap, and out-of-frame cropping clearer than RGB, but it omits doors, walls, furniture, and most objects, splits or merges some overlapping person regions, and cannot reliably provide metric depth, gaze, or front-versus-back orientation.
descriptions.pose: The pose map shows no detected body in frame 1, a small partial skeleton near center-right in frame 2, and progressively larger upper-body skeletons in frames 3–5, indicating approach toward the camera from roughly 1–2 m to well under 1 m. In frame 3, only a short shoulder/arm span and facial landmarks are recovered; in frame 4, the shoulders and both arms extend laterally, with the left wrist near the left side and the right wrist low-right, placing both arms near the camera wearer, while frame 5 shows one arm raised toward the upper left and the other extending right. Facial keypoints remain near the top-center of the foreground skeleton and are approximately directed toward the camera, although the sparse landmarks do not establish gaze precisely; other people visible in RGB are mostly absent because they are small or occluded. The pose map makes joint locations, limb direction, body scale change, and partial out-of-view limbs easier to read than RGB, but missing elbows, hands, torso/leg joints, occasional isolated keypoints, and absent background poses make reach, full orientation, and inter-person distances uncertain.
